s1.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
key_facts: Hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia
Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history reported
Developed blurred vision and redness in one eye on day 2 post-admission
Temporary pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma in the right eye
Normal complete blood cell counts
Normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with normal results
Fluorescein Angiography showed mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage

shortlist.label: COVID-19
shortlist.why_kept: Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement

shortlist.label: Optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision in the right eye

shortlist.label: Retinal vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fluorescein Angiography showed mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage and retinal vessel narrowing

shortlist.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Weakly positive IgG for VZV and ocular involvement

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Weakly positive IgG for CMV and retinal involvement

raw.rationale: The patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia and had recent close contact with a fatal case, with a positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, indicating COVID-19 infection. The development of blurred vision and redness in one eye, along with relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and other ocular findings, can be associated with COVID-19-related ocular complications.

rejected.label: Optic neuritis
rejected.why: While optic neuritis could explain some ocular findings, it does not account for the patient's pneumonia or the positive SARS-CoV-2 test.

rejected.label: Retinal vasculitis
rejected.why: Retinal vasculitis is present, but it is more likely a complication of the underlying condition rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
rejected.why: The patient had very weakly positive IgG for VZV, but this does not strongly support VZV retinitis as the primary diagnosis, especially with the context of COVID-19 infection.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
rejected.why: The patient had very weakly positive IgG for CMV, but CMV retinitis typically occurs in immunocompromised patients, and there is no indication of immunocompromise in this case beyond the COVID-19 infection itself.
